# AGent Energy Raises $11 Million In Series Seed Funding

STechCompanyNews.com helps you discover the latest insights on AI, venture funding, innovative companies, and the software tools shaping the future.

Houston-based AGent Energy secured $11 million in Series Seed funding (co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures) to scale its AI platform that aggregates and dispatches idle behind the meter backup generators into wholesale markets. [...] AGent Energy closed an $11 million Series Seed financing, co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures, with participation from Intrepid Investment Management and existing investors CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP). This brings the Houston-based company’s total capital raised to $17 million within its first 12 months of existence (following a $6 million seed round from CIV and ZIP that closed within two months of founding in 2025). The company positions the round as one of the fastest funding trajectories among distributed energy resource (DER) startups.

What is AGent Energy? [...] Investor and Governance Details

 Co-leads: Spero Ventures (Stephen Wemple joining the board) and MassMutual Ventures (Aram Ouligian as board observer).
 Participants: Intrepid Investment Management (energy focused private equity/infrastructure/venture investor) plus returning CIV and ZIP.

Investor commentary emphasizes speed of execution, the capital efficiency of unlocking existing assets versus new buildout (often multi year), and the combination of grid reliability, climate resilience, and immediate economics. Wemple noted the team has moved faster than any company observed in the space; Ouligian highlighted rapid response capability (minutes) with no new construction or owner cost.

## AGent Energy Raises $11 Million Series Seed Round

AGent Energy, an AI-driven distributed power plant developer in the behind-the-meter renewable energy market, has closed an $11 million Series Seed financing round co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures. The round brings the company’s total funding to $17 million within 12 months of its founding.

Intrepid Investment Management joined the round as a new investor, alongside existing backers CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP), which had provided AGent Energy’s earlier funding.

## Investors Back AGent Energy’s Growth

“Closing $17 million in our first year reflects both the urgency of the grid reliability challenge and the speed at which our team executes,” said Stephanie Hendricks, CEO and co-founder of AGent Energy. [...] Skip to content

.
 AGent Energy’s AI-based platform aggregates and dispatches distributed generation at commercial, industrial, and institutional sites, targeting more than 200 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity.
 The company currently dispatches generation in three North American wholesale power markets: PJM, MISO, and ERCOT.
 Stephen Wemple of Spero Ventures joins AGent Energy’s board of directors, and Aram Ouligian of MassMutual Ventures joins as a board observer.

## AGent Energy Raises $11 Million Series Seed Round [...] ### Board Changes and Market Reach

As part of the financing, Stephen Wemple joins AGent Energy’s board of directors, while Aram Ouligian, senior associate at MassMutual Ventures, joins as a board observer.

“When the grid is stressed, the difference between a rolling blackout and an ordinary afternoon is how fast dispatchable capacity shows up,” said Ouligian. “AGent’s AI platform turns generation already sitting at hospitals, universities, and industrial sites into exactly that: capacity that responds in minutes, with no new construction and no cost to the owner.”

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

AGent Energy, a startup that integrates backup generators into the grid during emergencies, raised $11 million in seed funding co-led by Spero Ventures and MassMutual Ventures.

Why it matters: Power demand is rising quickly, straining grids and helping drive up electricity bills. [...] Intrepid Investment Management and existing investors CIV and Zero Infinity Partners (ZIP) joined the new round. CIV and ZIP provided $6 million last year.
   The firm already operates in three markets, Hendricks said — Texas (ERCOT), the Midcontinent Independent System Operator region, and PJM.
   Its current portfolio is equivalent to the size of a small power plant, she said. 

Zoom out: AGent is one of multiple companies making use of distributed resources like solar and batteries to aid grids.

   The company argues that tapping backup generation "delivers capacity at the lowest cost of any new grid resource." [...] But building new power plants is often slow and expensive.
   AGent sees a big market in harnessing backup generators that sit mostly idle at farms, hospitals, factories, big box stores, universities and beyond.

How it works:The year-old startup provides hardware and software that remotely turns on backup generators when grids face emergencies.

   This displaces electricity demand at those sites, freeing up more power for the rest of the grid.
   Backup generators don't erase the need for new power plants, but could provide substantial breathing room.

"This is the fastest and most capital-efficient way to add new capacity to the grid," co-founder and CEO Stephanie Hendricks said, calling it a "massive underutilized resource."
